name: Stanford HAI AI Index: annual AI trends and data landing page
title: Stanford HAI AI Index: annual AI trends and data landing page
answer: The Stanford HAI AI Index is an annual, independent measurement program and landing page for data on artificial intelligence. It tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes AI data for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the public. Its most useful claim is that this year's Index reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, even as technical capabilities improve, investment accelerates, and adoption spreads. It says independent, rigorous measurement is increasingly critical because data transparency is declining.

sections.body: Stanford HAI publishes this AI Index landing page. It describes the AI Index as an independent initiative at Stanford HAI, led by an interdisciplinary steering committee. The page presents the program's mission, credibility claims, selected findings, people, and related work. It says this year's edition surpasses previous ones in size, scale, and scope. The harvested page is dated 2026-09-27 and refers to the 2026 Stanford AI Index Report released this month. It is a program overview rather than the full report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The AI Index says its mission is to provide unbiased, rigorously vetted, and globally sourced data for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the general public. It tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes data relating to artificial intelligence. This year's Index, according to the page, reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it. AI is integrating rapidly into the global economy, with technical capabilities improving, investment accelerating, and adoption spreading, but the frameworks needed to govern, evaluate, and understand the technology are falling behind. In a field where data transparency is declining, the page argues that independent, rigorous measurement has never been more critical. The page says the report provides the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available. It states that previous editions have been cited in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian, have amassed hundreds of academic citations, and have been referenced by high-level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. The program writes about AI progress and impact through a cross-sector lens, from research and development to technical performance, the economy, education, and policy. The page also mentions a paper on measuring AI systems and their impact, based on a fall 2019 Stanford workshop, with six summary challenges and over 40 presentations. It notes a collaboration with Dr. Elif Kiesow Cortez and The Hague University's AI & LegTech Lab on a judicial decision database.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that previous editions have amassed hundreds of academic citations and been cited in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian. It says they have been referenced by high-level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It describes a paper based on a fall 2019 Stanford workshop that identifies six summary challenges and summarizes over 40 presentations. It refers to the 2026 Stanford AI Index Report, released this month, and says this year's edition surpasses all previous ones in size, scale, and scope. It also says the report provides the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in nonprofits would use this source as a pointer to the AI Index's annual macro data and credibility claims, not as a nonprofit-specific study. The page says the Index covers AI's technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact through a cross-sector lens that includes education and policy. Its central claim, a widening gap between AI capability and preparedness to manage it, is relevant to mission-driven organizations weighing adoption against governance and evaluation capacity. The page also signals that independent measurement is becoming harder as data transparency declines, which matters for anyone citing AI trends in funding, policy, or program decisions.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Nonprofits

sections.body: This is a landing page, not the full AI Index report. It gives selected claims and links, with little methodology, no nonprofit-specific data, and no detailed sector breakdowns. It is published by Stanford HAI and relies on philanthropic support, so it is an institutional program page rather than independent journalism. The page is dated 2026-09-27 and refers to the 2026 report, but the harvested text is partial and repeats itself. It does not provide the underlying datasets, definitions, or confidence intervals needed to verify its numbers.
